tasks.short: Inventory or estimate plant and wildlife populations

steps.what: Choose the population, survey area, sampling method and effort needed for a defensible plant or wildlife inventory or estimate.
Survey the actual plots, transects or observation locations, identify plants or animals and assess detection conditions under the chosen protocol.
Capture actual species, counts, locations, effort and identification uncertainty in the existing field-recording software {OTHER}.

Build the inventory totals or selected population-estimation tables in {SPREADSHEET}; configure native observation tables, effort summaries and the scientist's chosen formulas, checking units, coverage and missing surveys.
Interpret the inventory or population estimate, test its assumptions and write and check the final findings and detectability limitations in {DOCS}.
Save the checked final population findings in {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Reuse native observation and effort tables in {SPREADSHEET} from actual field records in {OTHER}. The biologist chooses the sampling and estimation method, performs the survey and checks whether the result supports a population claim.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated observation grouping and effort calculations were rebuilt after each survey.
tasks.enabler_now: Native tables can reuse explicit species, location and effort fields with selected formulas.
tasks.still_hard: Species identification, incomplete detection and uneven sampling remain scientific problems.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a count of observations from a defensible population estimate.

ambition.what: No automatic population or conservation-status decision.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated survey arithmetic; fieldwork and method decisions remain.

evidence.claim: Native spreadsheet tables can group survey counts and effort while method choice and detectability assessment remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is the biologist's survey and estimate through its findings record, not a management plan or public presentation. Shares are a scenario, not measured labour.

The biologist produces survey ID, location, date and time, species or unresolved identification, count, effort, method and detection condition in s1-s3. Actual observation capture is fully counted; manual entry is the fallback. An unvisited location is missing, not a zero count.
Native field export and table configuration come first. Only repeated grouping and selected arithmetic lose time; field observation, source capture and scientific interpretation remain fully counted.
The ordinary final findings check in s5 binds the exact s6 document. Edits invalidate approval. Downstream tasks may reuse these findings but do not repeat this survey or its saving.
research_questions: Can the native table retain missed visits and effort separately from observed zero counts?

already_counted.description: Check survey grouping, effort and estimation calculations.

incremental.description: Validate tables and formulas when survey protocols change.

approvals.approved_version: Final population findings checked at the end of s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native reuse removes 45% of the 20-hour calculation share: 9 gross hours less 2 upkeep. Zero if already configured. Fieldwork, source capture and final interpretation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Choose the supported findings, sources and communication purpose for the report and talk, considering the school, club, interest group or park-programme audience and sensitive wildlife locations.

Prepare report figures, references and presentation layouts using native {DOCS} styles and reusable figure placements, checking captions and existing result references without rerunning the underlying research analysis.

Write the report and prepared presentation remarks; after native sections are reused, use a bounded prose draft from the verified source pack and check each claim, number, citation and explanation against the originals.

loop.purpose: Draft audience-appropriate wording of already supported wildlife findings.
loop.input: Selected source passages and finding IDs, existing figure references and audience brief.
loop.output: Report prose and prepared talk remarks with a source pointer for each factual claim.
loop.check: The biologist checks every claim and citation against the originals, including uncertainty, causality, population scope, sensitive location disclosure and whether simplification changes the science.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction at most, then manual writing. Missing sources stop drafting; no invented citations or direct publishing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native layout and citation fields handle structure first. Variable explanations for a particular audience require language drafting, followed by full scientific checking.

steps.what: Review and correct the complete report, slides and prepared remarks for scientific accuracy, clarity and permitted disclosure, then approve the final package and intended recipients and talk audience.
Save the checked final report and presentation package in {DOCS}.
Send the exact checked report to the intended recipients through {EMAIL}.
Give the prepared talk and presentation to the intended audience and respond personally to questions, preserving scientific limits rather than improvising unsupported claims.

tasks.design: Reuse native layouts and references in {DOCS}, then use a bounded source-linked draft for remaining prose. The biologist verifies the science and complete package before report delivery and the prepared presentation; the live talk and questions retain full time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated layouts, citations and first prose drafts consumed communication preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document features handle structure, while constrained language drafting can propose wording from selected evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Accessible explanation must not erase uncertainty or expose sensitive wildlife locations.
tasks.human_edge: Explain why the findings matter and answer an audience's actual questions responsibly.

ambition.what: Prepare a school-facing explanation from an existing technical report, if the time reduction is realised.

tasks.altitude: More preparation capacity for public explanation without reducing the live engagement.

evidence.claim: A bounded language draft can propose explanations from supplied findings but needs scientific source checking.

assumptions: This instance covers a written report and accompanying public talk. Journal-specific submission, coauthor approvals and underlying research are separate unchanged processes. Shares are illustrative, not measured.

The biologist supplies finding ID, source passage, figure ID, uncertainty statement, citation reference, audience and disclosure restriction in s1-s3. Existing research authors produce the checked results and figures. Manual selection and checking are retained; missing sources require manual writing or omission, never fabricated support.

Native layouts and references come first. Only communication preparation loses time; no second saving for research calculations is counted. No additional data collection or figure-analysis work is transferred for free.

s4's ordinary final package check binds its exact version, report recipients and prepared talk audience for s5-s7. Changes require recheck. The talk gate covers prepared material; live questions remain human judgement with their full time retained.
unknowns: Existing layout reuse and draft correction effort
Actual demand for a school-facing explanation
research_questions: Does source checking preserve a preparation gain when explaining uncertainty to non-specialists?

already_counted.description: Check communication layouts, references and all drafted scientific statements.

incremental.description: Maintain layouts and review draft errors when source formats change.

approvals.approved_version: Final communication package checked at the end of s4
Same final report and recipients checked at the end of s4, unchanged by s5
Final presentation, prepared remarks and intended audience checked at the end of s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native layout reuse saves 8.75 hours and source-checked prose drafting 7 hours per 100 baseline hours, less 3 upkeep: 12.75 net. Zero if already streamlined or correction erases gains. Final review, save, send and all 19 hours of live presentation remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop wildlife and habitat management recommendations

steps.what: Review wildlife population and habitat evidence, management objectives and applicable constraints before developing options.
Consult stakeholders and the public to explore wildlife and habitat options, understand concerns and discuss the evidence and trade-offs.
Record the actual options discussed, differing views, unresolved questions and source references in {DOCS}, without representing consultation as agreement.
Develop the management system or recommendations, weighing ecological effects, uncertainty, feasibility and stakeholder concerns; choose monitoring and review conditions.

Assemble the final management plan in {DOCS}; configure native headings, evidence-reference fields and monitoring tables, then write and check all recommendations and consultation representations in the completed version.
Save the checked final habitat management plan in {DOCS}.
Send the exact stored plan to the checked management-plan recipients through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure native plan headings, reference fields and monitoring tables in {DOCS}. The biologist retains consultation, records its actual contributions and develops the ecological recommendations; the completed plan is checked before separate save and delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan repeatedly rebuilt evidence references and monitoring-table structure.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document templates can preserve chosen reference and monitoring fields without making ecological decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Competing land uses and uncertain habitat effects cannot be resolved by a document template.
tasks.human_edge: Weigh ecological evidence and public concerns without falsely presenting consensus.

ambition.what: No new authority to implement habitat interventions.

tasks.altitude: Small document-assembly savings; consultation and recommendation decisions remain.

evidence.claim: Native document templates can reuse plan structure and evidence fields while management recommendations remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is preparing and delivering recommendations, not stakeholder decision-making or implementation. The habitat mapping software {OTHER} supplies existing habitat evidence. Shares are illustrative.

The biologist verifies source IDs, population and habitat findings, objectives and constraints in s1, captures actual consultation option, contributor, concern and unresolved issue in s3, and chooses recommendation, rationale and monitoring trigger in s4. Manual capture and checking remain counted. Other participants' time is unchanged and excluded from focal savings.

Native templates come first. Only repeated layout and reference assembly lose time; all ecological reasoning, actual consultation notes and recommendation wording remain counted. Upstream population surveys are inputs, not a second saving.
s5's ordinary author check covers the completed plan and recipient list for s6-s7. Edits invalidate both approvals. Delivery is advice, not authority to carry out an intervention.
unknowns: Actual consultation and management authority boundaries
research_questions: Can the native plan structure retain dissent and evidence limitations beside each recommendation?

already_counted.description: Write and check the completed plan and consultation representations.

incremental.description: Maintain plan reference and monitoring-table configuration.

approvals.approved_version: Final habitat management plan checked at the end of s5
Same final plan and intended recipients checked at the end of s5, unchanged by s6

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native plan assembly removes 25% of the 13-hour assembly share: 3.25 gross hours less 1 upkeep. Zero with templates already used. Consultation, note capture, recommendations, save and send retain their stated time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study industrial effects on animals and recommend alternatives

steps.what: Define the habitat and animal-response question, review existing environmental and industrial operating records, and choose the observation and comparison methods.
Study animals in their natural habitat and observe the actual environmental conditions and industrial exposure relevant to the question.
Capture the actual animal observations, locations, times, environmental readings and uncertainty in the field-recording software {OTHER}.
Compare actual observations with selected operating conditions using native {SPREADSHEET} time-alignment tables and plots, checking units, coverage, gaps and the chosen comparison windows.
Interpret environmental and industrial effects on the animals, assess alternative explanations and recommend supported alternative operating conditions with explicit limits.
outputs: supported impact findings and operating recommendations

steps.what: Write and check the final impact-study report, its evidence references, uncertainty and operating recommendations, including the intended recipient list.
inputs: supported impact findings and operating recommendations

steps.what: Save the checked final impact-study report in {DOCS}.
Send the exact stored impact-study report and recommendations to the checked recipients through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure native time-alignment and comparison plots in {SPREADSHEET} from actual field observations in {OTHER} and existing operating records. The biologist retains habitat study, causal interpretation and recommendation writing, then checks and delivers the completed report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated alignment and plotting of observation and operating periods consumed analysis preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native tables can reuse explicit timestamps, units and selected comparison windows.
tasks.still_hard: Confounding, seasonal effects and incomplete exposure information limit causal conclusions.
tasks.human_edge: Recommend only operating alternatives supported by the actual evidence and acknowledge uncertainty.

ambition.what: Inspect a second explicitly chosen operating-period comparison before finalising the recommendation.

tasks.altitude: Less comparison setup leaves more time for alternative explanations, without authority to change industrial operations.

evidence.claim: Native spreadsheet tables can align explicit observation and operating timestamps for comparison plots without determining causation.

assumptions: Boundary is a study of animal response and industrial exposure through its recommendation report, distinct from the general population inventory and habitat plan. No duplicate survey or calculation credit is counted. Shares are illustrative.

The biologist captures study ID, animal or observation reference, location, actual time, response, environmental value and unit, method and uncertainty in s2-s3. Existing industrial record producers supply operating timestamp, condition and source reference; the biologist verifies them in s1 and s4. Manual entry and clarification remain counted. Missing or incomparable periods remain explicit gaps.

Native tables and plotting are tried first. Only repeated alignment and plotting lose time; fieldwork, first capture, causal interpretation and report writing remain fully counted. No change in animal welfare or industrial output is quantified.
s6's ordinary author check approves the final report and recipients for s7-s8. Edits invalidate both approvals. Delivery is advice, not a command to change operating conditions.
unknowns: Availability and comparability of operating records
research_questions: Can native plots preserve missing observations and differing timestamp conventions visibly?

already_counted.description: Check observation alignment and comparison plots.

incremental.description: Maintain timestamp and unit mappings for comparison tables.

approvals.approved_version: Final impact-study report checked at the end of s6
Same final report and recipients checked at the end of s6, unchanged by s7

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native alignment and plots remove 30% of the 15-hour comparison share: 4.5 gross hours less 1 upkeep. Zero if already configured. Physical study, actual records, interpretation, report, save and send retain their stated time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Wildlife biologists retain field observation, ecological interpretation and public consultation while native tables and checked communication drafts reduce repeated preparation.
reach: Improve observation protocols with biological technicians
Assess intervention uncertainty with conservation scientists
role.ambitious_version: Make findings easier to inspect and communicate without substituting generated claims for field evidence or public consultation.
